stem_book: A uniform thin flat isolated disc is floating in space (initially at rest). It has radius R and mass m. A force F is applied to it in the y-direction at a distance d = R/2 from the centre (to the right of the centre, as shown). Treat this problem as two-dimensional. At the instant shown the: (a) acceleration of the center of the disc is F/m. (b) angular acceleration of the disk is F/mR. (c) acceleration of leftmost point on the disc is zero. (d) point which is instantaneously unaccelerated is the rightmost point.
key: a, b, c a cm = F/m, α = F/mR, leftmost point unaccelerated
reason: added 'initially at rest' (ω = 0, so no centripetal term) and the side of the force from the figure
work: a_cm = F/m; α = F(R/2)/(mR²/2) = F/(mR); leftmost: F/m − αR = 0 (c); rightmost: 2F/m (d false)
